entries.test: Whether the text of SB-1047 (as amended by August 2024) requires developers to anticipate every possible use of their models, or only to take reasonable care against specified critical harms.
entries.note: This is a claim about what the bill text says, so the bill text can settle it.

Marcus wrote that the provisions 'seem reasonable to me' and that he doesn't 'understand what would justify an exemption.' The record turns this into a flat statement that no exemption is justified, which is firmer than what he said.

entries.test: Whether the SB-1047 text at the time sets a duty of reasonable safeguards or reasonable care against critical harms, rather than requiring those harms to be fully prevented.
entries.note: The bill's exact wording ('reasonable assurance' vs 'reasonable care') changed between amendments.

entries.test: Compare SB-1047's requirements with the July 2023 White House voluntary AI commitments and the May 2024 Seoul Frontier AI Safety Commitments to see whether much of what the bill requires overlaps with them.
entries.note: 'Much of' is loose, but most readers would agree on how to make the comparison.

entries.test: Whether the August 2024 amended text of SB-1047 limits the full-shutdown requirement to covered models still under the developer's control.
entries.note: The proposition drops his hedge 'as I understand' and states the point flatly. The hedge appears only in the conditions field.

entries.test: Whether SB-1047's main obligations apply only to covered models whose training compute costs more than $100 million.
entries.note: The proposition drops 'presumably' and states the 'not little tech' inference flatly. Only the $100M threshold can really be checked.
This is a stated personal position in favour of the bill.

entries.test: Whether pharmaceuticals, aviation, and automobiles are subject to required safety evaluation against set standards (e.g., FDA approval, FAA certification, FMVSS).
entries.note: Marcus is describing practice in other industries, not saying in this sentence what AI regulation should be. The drafter added a normative 'is reasonable' that is not in his words.
